chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from al-Husayn ibn Sayf, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu al-Fawaris, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbade me from speaking between the four Rak'at which are after Maghrib.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the optional prayers after Maghrib?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the etiquette of khushu' (devotional focus) during the four Rak'at of optional prayer following Maghrib, a practice often associated with the Prophet's tradition. The prohibition of speech during this interval underscores the importance of maintaining spiritual concentration and transitioning from the communal Maghrib prayer to individual devotion. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a basis for distinguishing between the prayer itself and the interval, emphasizing mindfulness over casual conversation.
